clue.text: Get the woman the highest profit or the lowest

parts.note: to net is to get or earn as clear gain
her is the pronoun for a woman
the most is the greatest amount, the highest return

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to make a woman earn top returns or bottom ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'profit' seems to pair with 'Get' as an idea of earning, but it belongs with 'the highest' to give MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic superlative of nether, meaning lowest or furthest down, as in the deepest regions.

clue.text: It breathes and is conscious, we're told

indicators.note: something we are told is heard, so the word for being conscious is said out loud

parts.note: to be conscious of something is to know it, so 'knows'

explanation.surface: A riddle about a living thing that breathes and is aware.
explanation.definitionFit: The facial organ through which a person or animal draws in air, so it is what breathes.

clue.text: Does it make sailing quite a business?

definitions.text: Does it make sailing quite a business?

parts.words: Does it make sailing quite a business
parts.note: the air that drives sailing ships, read as the breeze of commerce

explanation.definitionFit: A steady tropical wind that historically carried merchant sailing ships, so it is wind tied to commerce.

clue.text: Praise, for once, given to the tyro

parts.note: ex means former, what something was once
taken as written
L for learner, a beginner or tyro

explanation.surface: For once someone gives warm words to a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud or speak highly of someone, a formal synonym for commending.

clue.text: Newspapers and TV by the time I'm leaving intervene

parts.note: the press and broadcasting together are the media

indicators.note: the clue says the letters of I'm walk out of the word time, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: taken as the word to be cut

explanation.surface: The press and television step in just as I'm on my way out.
explanation.definitionFit: To come between disputing parties to help reach agreement, the sense of stepping in.

clue.text: They reckon they're heading for a fall

definitions.meaning: people who sum or add up figures
warm seasons that lead into autumn, which Americans call fall

explanation.definitionFit: One reading is people who do sums; the other is the warm seasons that come before autumn.

clue.text: Long article on a chess opening

parts.note: an article is a thing or item, so 'it'
the opening two letters of the word chess

explanation.surface: A lengthy piece of writing about one way to begin a game of chess.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to have a restless craving or yearning for it.

clue.text: Detectives in evening dress?

definitions.meaning: detectives who follow suspects are said to tail them
a formal tailcoat worn as men's evening dress

explanation.definitionFit: Followers shadowing a suspect are tails; a tailcoat for formal evening wear is also called tails.

clue.text: Watch parts or part of a gymnastic act

parts.note: a watch has hands on its face
a mainspring drives a mechanical watch

explanation.surface: Pieces of a timepiece, or a section of a gymnast's routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A gymnastic move in which one springs over onto the hands and back to the feet.

clue.text: Convinced it was measured wrongly

indicators.note: something done wrongly is put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was sure the thing had been measured incorrectly.
explanation.definitionFit: To have checked and become certain, so to be convinced of something.

clue.text: Have the point sharp, to begin with

parts.note: S for south, a point of the compass
a tart taste is sharp or sour

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a pointed tip keen from the very outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To commence or set out, the same infinitive sense as beginning.

clue.text: Blast the horse race!

parts.note: an oath read as damning the Grand National, Britain's best-known steeplechase

explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is a famous British horse race, so cursing it is damning the National.
explanation.definitionFit: An expression of annoyance or a curse, the same angry sense as blast.

clue.text: A congenial one helps to while the time away

definitions.text: A congenial one helps to while the time away

parts.words: A congenial one helps to while the time away
parts.note: time here is a prison sentence, made easier by a friendly companion in the cell

explanation.definitionFit: A fellow prisoner sharing a cell, someone serving time alongside you.

clue.text: Becomes less severe and one moves gingerly

definitions.meaning: pain or pressure lessens or abates
one inches something carefully into place

explanation.definitionFit: It means both lessens or relents and manoeuvres something slowly and carefully.

clue.text: Peeps through the window in the early morning

definitions.text: Peeps through the window in the early morning

parts.words: Peeps through the window in the early morning
parts.note: peeps are the cheeps of birds heard at first light, not glances

explanation.definitionFit: The chorus of birdsong heard at first light, the birds' peeping heard at daybreak.

clue.text: A charming "Can I do it?

parts.note: asking if one can is asking 'am I'
able means fit to do it

explanation.surface: A pleasant person asks politely whether they are up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The question 'Am I able?' is another way to ask 'Can I do it?'
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and good-natured, a close synonym for pleasant and likeable.

clue.text: Nothing's up. The ship is catching fish

indicators.note: the vessel catches, so holds inside it, the reversed word

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: nil's, with nothing being nil

explanation.surface: Nothing is happening as a ship hauls in its catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A small herring-like sea fish, the sprat, often tinned as sardines.

clue.text: He pronounces to be fitter

definitions.meaning: one who sounds or utters words

explanation.definitionFit: Both one who voices a word and the comparative of sound, meaning healthier.

clue.text: The lad is wrong. The girl is hiding in the boot

indicators.note: the girl hides inside the rearranged letters
letters gone wrong are put out of order

parts.note: a miss is a young girl

explanation.surface: A boy is mistaken, and a girl is lurking inside a car's luggage space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The boot' looks like footwear or a car's luggage space, but getting the boot is British slang for being sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting the boot is slang for being sacked, so it means being fired from a job.

clue.text: Agreeing it's only casual as acquaintances go

definitions.meaning: bobbing the head to say yes
a ... acquaintance is someone known only slightly

explanation.definitionFit: Both bowing the head in assent and describing someone known only slightly, as in a nodding acquaintance.

clue.text: Fools about, on return, with an Italian

indicators.note: the silly birds go about, so around, the reversed word

parts.note: geese are proverbially silly, so fools

indicators.note: returning means the little word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Idiots fooling about with an Italian on their way back.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Genoa, the port city in northwest Italy.

clue.text: Continue to recruit forcibly?

definitions.meaning: to press men was to force them into naval service, and on adds continuation

explanation.definitionFit: It means to keep going regardless, and jokingly to impress men into service.

clue.text: He reads through, sure it's wrong

parts.note: per means through or by means of

indicators.note: being wrong, the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A reader is confident that something is mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies a text closely, one who reads it carefully.

clue.text: Call by telephone to get accommodation

definitions.meaning: the code word for H in the radio phonetic alphabet used over the phone
a place offering rooms for travellers

explanation.definitionFit: It is the call word for H in the phonetic alphabet and a place to stay the night.

clue.text: Playtime

parts.note: the time or speed at which music is played

explanation.definitionFit: The speed or pace of a piece of music, its rate of performance.

clue.text: Drug from the Arctic, on order

indicators.note: putting the letters in a fresh order rearranges them

explanation.surface: A drug smuggled from the far north, on request.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that dulls the senses or induces sleep, often an illegal drug.

clue.text: To get round, over tips a little

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a bit is a little amount

explanation.surface: To manage, someone hands out slightly more than they should.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit is to circle around something, as a moon does a planet.

clue.text: What's in the trunk, would you say?

indicators.note: said by you, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: taken as the word spoken

explanation.surface: A question about what a trunk contains, asking for your view.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber makes up the trunk of a tree, so it is the material within.

clue.text: They don't let us forget about the German miners being out

indicators.note: turned about, the letters are moved around
out means out of place, so rearranged

parts.note: der is the German for the

explanation.surface: Notices about German miners on strike keep everyone informed.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompts or notes that jog the memory, keeping something in mind.

clue.text: Man singing "One Fish Ball"

parts.note: bass is a kind of fish
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: Looks like the title of a song performed by a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A male singer with a low voice, the Italian word for bass.

clue.text: Go away," said with a brogue?

indicators.note: the word is spoken aloud, so heard not read

parts.note: shoo is what one says to send someone away

explanation.surface: Someone told to leave in an Irish accent.
explanation.walkthrough: A brogue is both an Irish accent and a sturdy leather footwear style; it is the second sense that defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogue is a type of sturdy leather footwear with decorative perforations.

clue.text: Be upset by the ride in the old jalopy?

definitions.text: Be upset by the ride in the old jalopy?

parts.words: Be upset by the ride in the old jalopy
parts.note: be flustered, or literally be shaken about in a rickety car

explanation.definitionFit: It means become flustered, and literally be shaken by a bumpy car journey.
